messages.subject_clean: dplyr: Methods for effficient selection of top row in groups
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

A little background:
What I'm trying to do is simply: Group a tbl on a variable, and select the top row in each group (similar to the "mult = 'first'" approach in data.table).

To solve the problem, I started by using the following syntax (using dplyr 0.1.3.99 as of today, April 3):
MyData %.% group_by(myVar) %.% filter(row_number(myVar) ==1)

but that takes a ridiculously long time on a big table (I'm using a 8M row by 7 column tbl_dt).

I've also tried one of the alternative approaches:
MyData %.% group_by(myVar) %.% filter(1:n() == 1)
or
MyData %.% group_by(myVar) %.% filter(row_number() == 1)

but this throws the following errors, respectively:

"Error in n() : This function should not be called directly"
and
"Error in rank(x, ties.method = "first") :
  argument "x" is missing, with no default"

So now to my question:
It would seem to me that the filter query can be greatly simplified by simply passing the number of the row I want to select as an argument - i.e., using the following query:
MyData %.% group_by(myVar) %.% filter(1)

Is this the desired behavior? And if not - why is that so? It would seem to me that the "1:n()" syntax would simply return a vector of numbers, so why not simply use the first number?

Cheers,
Love Hansson

library(dplyr) ## v0.1.3
library(data.table) ## v1.9.2

df <- data.frame(
  Id=1:10000000,
  MyVar=sample(10000000, replace = TRUE),
  someDate=as.POSIXct(sample(10000000, replace = TRUE), origin = Sys.Date()))

              group_by(MyVar) %.%
              filter(row_number(MyVar) == 1))

dt <- as.data.table(df)
system.time(fd.dt <- dt[ dt[, .I[1], by='MyVar']$V1 ])
##  user  system elapsed
## 4.227   0.397   4.752

all.equal(fd.dp, as.data.frame(fd.dt))
## [1] TRUE

Hello, I'm a beginner with dplyr and am having trouble using quantile() with summarize. I am working with a grouped data set. I want to get the nth, 50th and (100-n)th quantile for the variable score.diff for each group.

When I use more than one value for the arguments to p= in quantile (e.g., p=c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9)) summarize tells me
Error: expecting a single value
So, I did three separate summarize calls like this:

conf.int <http://conf.int> <- 0.9
intervals <- as.data.frame(summarize(grouped.ts, quantile(score.diff, p=conf.int <http://conf.int>)))
intervals$med <- summarize(grouped.ts, quantile(score.diff, p=0.5))
intervals$bot <- summarize(grouped.ts, quantile(score.diff, p=1-conf.int <http://1-conf.int>))

But the structure of the resulting data frame is very peculiar, so in order to reference intervals$med and intervals$bot I have to use intervals$med[,2].

Can someone give me some guidance?
TIA.
--

ddply(d, .(S), summarize, M=mean(var), Med=median(var),  Q=matrix(quantile (var, probs=c(0.25,0.50,0.75)) ,ncol=3) )

# However the equivalent does not seem to work with dplyr, unfortunately

library(dplyr)

d %.% group_by(S) %.%
  summarise(M=mean(var), Med=median(var), Q= matrix(quantile (var, probs=c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75) ), ncol=3) )
# Error: expecting a single value

Here is a workaround
d %.% group_by(S) %.%
  summarise(M=mean(var), Med=median(var), Q1=quantile (var, probs=0.25), Q2=quantile (var, probs=0.50), Q3=quantile(var, probs=0.75))

Alain

  c("Year", "Month", "DayofMonth"), "UniqueCarrier", "TailNum"))

hflights2 <- compute(mutate(hflights, speed = AirTime / Distance), name = "hflights2")
db

src:  sqlite 3.7.17 [db.sqlite3]
tbls: hflights, hflights2, sqlite_stat1

I would like to keep the `hflights2` table in the database even after I exit the R session. Is there a decent way to achieve this? It seems as though `compute` will only create a temporary copy of this table (that is, the table is removed from the database upon exiting).

Thanks,

-Carson

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

As I started exploring dplyr, I found some unexpected differences between plyr and dplyr that I would like to clarify and understand whether this is intentional or not, and whether there are alternative solutions

Thanks

Two things :

1. mutate can't handle multiple outputs

# generate a set of observations : 100 obs per category
nobs <- 100
ncat <- 5
cat  <- letters[1:ncat]
data <-  data.frame (cat= rep(cat, each=nobs), val=round(rnorm(nobs*ncat, mean=100,sd=20 ), 0))

# ddply & sumarize works fine
require(plyr)
ddply(data, .(cat), summarise, m= mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))
plyr::summarize(data, m = mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))

# ddply & transform work fine
require(plyr)
ddply(data, .(cat),transform, m= mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))
transform(data, m = mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))

# but neither plyr::mutate nor dplyr::mutate do

require(plyr)
ddply(data, .(cat), mutate, m= mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))
> Error : wrong result size (11), expected 100 or 1

plyr::mutate(data, m = mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))
> Error in `[[<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, col, value = c(36, 75, 81, 88, 93,  :
  replacement has 1 row, data has 500

require(dplyr)
group_by(data, cat) %.% mutate(m=mean(val))
> OK
group_by(data, cat) %.% mutate(Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))
> Error : incompatible size (11), expecting 100 (the group size) or 1

# 2. dplyr::mutate can't handle reference to external tables

# 2. dplyr::mutate can't handle reference to external tables ?

nobs <- 100
ncat <- 5
cat  <- letters[1:ncat]
CAT <-  data.frame(catname=cat, catval = c(10,20,30,40, 50))
data <-  data.frame (num= 1:500, cat= rep(cat, each=nobs),  val=round(rnorm(nobs*ncat, mean=100,sd=20 ), 0))

# this works fine :
data2  <- ddply(data,.(num), mutate, valcat= CAT$catval[CAT$catname==cat])
#
# but this does not :
require(dplyr)
mutate (data, valcat= CAT$catval[CAT$catname==cat])
> Error: wrong result size (100), expected 500 or 1
data2 <- data%.% group_by(num) %.% mutate (valcat= CAT$catval[CAT$catname==cat])
> Error: incompatible size (5), expecting 1 (the group size) or 1

# However, the following does work !
fc <-  function(c) CAT$catval[CAT$catname==c]
data2 <- data%.% group_by(num) %.% mutate (valcat= fc(cat))

Thanks

Alain

messages.subject: cumany bug when evaluating NA?
messages.subject_clean: cumany bug when evaluating NA?
messages.body_plain:
I encountered some strange behavior from the function cumany().  It also appears to happen with cumall().  It seems that if any of the prior values is NA, cumany and cumall return TRUE.  I assume this is a bug?  This is an issue for me because I'm trying to use cumany in conjunction with lag and the combined result is that everything evaluates to TRUE.

> cumany(c(NA, NA, NA)==1)
[1]   NA TRUE TRUE
> cumall(c(NA, NA, NA)==1)
[1]   NA TRUE TRUE

On the command line, na.omit seems to solve the problem:

> cumany(lag(c(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0))==1)
[1]   NA TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE
> cumany(na.omit(lag(c(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)))==1)
[1] FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE

However that breaks inside of mutate which is expecting an additional value.  I have discovered I can get around this by padding in a starting value, but that's a very kludgy solution.

> df = data.frame(id=c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B"),
+            val=c(0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1))
> df %.% group_by(id) %.% mutate(x = c(NA, cumany(na.omit(lag(val))==1)))
Source: local data frame [6 x 3]
Groups: id

  id val     x
1  A   0    NA
2  A   1 FALSE
3  A   0  TRUE
4  B   0    NA
5  B   0 FALSE
6  B   1 FALSE

-Andrew

> df <- data.frame(x=-1:5)
> z <- c(3,4)
>
> subset(df, x > min(z))
x
4
5

x
1
2
3
4
5
> dplyr::filter(df, x > base::min(z))
x
4
5
> dplyr::filter(df, x > max(z))
x
5
>
